artworks.title: "Athena Rescuing a Youth From Idleness"
artworks.artist: Hugues Taravai, Jules Allard et ses Fils (designer)
artworks.description:
"Athena Rescuing a Youth From Idleness" by Hugues Taravai (French, 1729-1785), an octagonal shaped oil on canvas allegorical ceiling painting installed on the Gold Room / Ballroom ceiling of Marble House. The painting represents Pallas Athena wearing her helmet and breastplate, accompanied by her attribute, the owl, and carrying aloft a youth (in the Florentine original representing an adolescent prince Ferdinand II of Medici) who is bidding farewell to a reclining female figure representing Venus, as Cupid grasps his ankle.

Venus is seated with two female attendants on a draped couch with a drapery at its rear secured to a tree. To the right, a blue toga clad female figure looks out at the viewer to engage one in the scene. Behind her, two satyr vessel bearers and a female cup bearer approach the couch.

The canvas is after a 16th century Italian original by Pietro da Cortona in the Palazzo Pitti, Florence, copied in turn by Hugues Taraval in the late 18th century.

This piece was originally the ceiling painting in the salon of the marquise de Pompignan in the Hotel de Clermont, 69, rue de Varenne, Paris and ordered by the Comte d'Orsay for his mother the marquise circa 1778 after an engraving of the Italian original by da Cortona

artworks.title: Pastiglia Cassone
artworks.dimensions: H 29.5 inches · W 71.5 inches · D 23.25 inches
artworks.description:
A Pastiglia cassone attributed to the workshop of Francesco di Giorgio, Sienna, Italy, possibly executed with the help of Neroccio de’ Landi (Italian, 1447-1500). The cassone, or marriage chest, is extensively decorated on all sides with gilded pastiglia (low relief plasterwork modeled in gesso and gilded) and rests on a series of arched bracket feet.

On the front a border of undulating vines, with painted highlights, surrounds an oblong low relief panel depicting a wedding procession. At the ends of the panel, standing winged figures are wearing armor and hold shields painted with coats of arms. The field on which the figures stand as well as the emblazoned shields and armorials are painted with blue highlights. The back is unfinished and the gilded surface and punchwork are the work of a 19th century restorer.
artworks.credit: Purchased by the Preservation Society of Newport County, 2014.

artworks.title: "The Erythraean and Cumaen Sibyls"
artworks.description: A Gothic tapestry representing "The Erythraean and Cumaen Sibyls". The tapestry depicts the Gothic theme of the secret garden. Centered by a sacred fountain, symbolic of the divine word, a dense foliate field sprouts roses (symbolizing the virgin) and poppies (symbolizing the earth). Two sibyls, prophetesses announcing the coming of Christ, stand to the left and right, while at their feet sit a unicorn (a symbol of purity and Jesus) and a griffin (also a symbol of Jesus, as well as the uniting of the terrestrial and the aerial).
artworks.credit: Bequest of Mrs. Gertrude Conaway Vanderbilt, 1979.
